title: Quarterly update Q&A cribsheet (rapid-fire)
body:
Quick cribsheet for the townhall Q&A. Tone: candid, engineering-first, avoid hard dates for product roadmaps. Keep answers short (30–60s) and call out follow-ups when the question needs a deeper dive.

Structure:
- 2 min: company health snapshot (Leah)
- 3 min: product highlights (me)
- 10–15 min: live Q&A (open floor + pre-seeded questions)

Pre-seeded Qs (with short answers / follow-ups):
1) "How are we doing on latency / reliability SLAs for Dedicated customers?"
- Short: "We hit our committed 99.9% uptime target for committed pools last quarter; p95 latency improved ~18% after the new batching heuristics."
- If they press: call out tradeoffs: "Improvements were mostly for steady-state workloads; tail latency for bursty single-tenant spikes still needs work — SRE + serving runtime have a focused project (see JIRA-3289) to shorten cold-starts and KV cache warmup."
- Follow-up: offer a deeper doc + data: link to per-customer SLA dashboard (post-townhall).

2) "Any changes to pricing or credit policy we should expect?"
- Short: "No immediate headline pricing changes. We'll continue to iterate on packaging (e.g., more flexible burst add-ons for Dedicated) and will communicate any changes with 30+ day notice and migration guidance."
- Follow-up: if asked about cost for large models, explain Optimize recommendations are being piloted with select customers to reduce token costs without degrading quality.

3) "What’s the status of Private / VPC on-prem rollouts for regulated customers?"
- Short: "We're onboarding two pilots this quarter with gov/health customers; Private v1 delivered the control-plane, next month we’re shipping the HSM/KMS integration."
- Follow-up: avoid specific timelines — defer to solutions-eng for commitments.

4) "We saw a recent incident — what happened and what’s changed?"
- Short: "Root cause: autoscaler misconfiguration + a degraded monitoring alert pathway. Fixes: autoscaler guardrails, additional tracing, and a new runbook. We also added a postmortem with action items shared to SRE + Platform channels."
- If asked for impact numbers: have rough metrics ready (e.g., % of requests affected, time window).

5) "How are we prioritizing model quality vs cost optimizations?"
- Short: "We treat quality as primary for customer-facing endpoints; Optimize tooling is targeted to workloads where customers can trade small latency/quality changes for large cost savings. We annotate regressions and gate any rollout with eval suites."

6) "Hiring / headcount question: are we still hiring aggressively?"
- Short: "Yes, we’re hiring in critical areas (SRE, serving runtime, sales engineering) but we’re more deliberate than last year — focusing on roles that impact latency and customer onboarding."

7) "How do we think about fallback to cheaper models during capacity pressure?"
- Short: "Smart routing + compatible model variants are in prod — requests are routed by policy (latency-first vs cost-first). We’re conservative with fallbacks for customer-critical routes and provide explicit opt-in for aggressive cost fallbacks."

Ad-lib prompts (one-liners):
- "We’re optimizing for predictable economics, not just raw throughput."
- "Feedback from early Dedicated customers shaped our new autoscaler guardrails."
- "No product date promises today — we’ll share milestones when features reach a customer-ready beta."

Notes-to-self / moderation cues:
- If someone pushes for a date, bridge: "We’ll take this offline and capture the ask — can you file a Jira so SRE/product can respond with specifics?"
- Avoid detailed infra configs in a public forum; point to runbooks or follow-up threads.
- If a competitor comparison comes up, emphasize differentiators: unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, strong observability, rollout controls.

Unresolved / items to lock before townhall:
- Confirm SLA language copy with Legal (Leah) — deadline: 2026-03-11.
- Get final incident postmortem link and one-paragraph summary from SRE (Ben) — deadline: 2026-03-11.
- Short explainer (1 slide) for Optimize pilots: success metrics + a customer vignette (Product) — deadline: 2026-03-11.

Follow-ups to offer after the townhall:
- Deep-dive office hours next week for customers & internal teams (SRE + Serving Runtime).
- Link to a living FAQ doc with answers + data (I’ll draft and circulate).

Checklist for prep (myself):
- [ ] Bullet slides (2 slides): product wins + incident summary
- [ ] One-liner for each pre-seeded Q
- [ ] Slack pre-announce with 3 prompts to seed the Q&A channel
- [ ] Confirm mic and recording with events ops

Tone reminders: be transparent but scoped — share what we know, what we’re fixing, and concrete next steps. Avoid committing to dates on-stage. Always offer a clear follow-up path (Jira/office hours/doc).

End of cribsheet. Keep this doc lightweight — I’ll convert the finalized lines into the speaker slide deck tomorrow.

---
Notes to self (scratch):
- Possible tough Q to prep: "Which large open models are we endorsing / deprecating?" -> safe answer: "We maintain a curated catalog; model recommendations are based on workload metrics and are subject to change as the ecosystem evolves."
- Keep 1–2 customer anecdotes ready (anonymized) about cost reduction using Optimize.
- Remember to thank product + SRE on-stage for fast incident response.
